content_units: Ireland Contractor Intake: What to Collect

Use this checklist to update a simple onboarding form for freelance contractors working with your nonprofit clinic in Dublin. Keep it practical and limited to information needed for setup, payment, compliance, confidentiality, and recordkeeping.
Option 1: Identity and contact details   Confirm who the contractor is and how to reach them   Core admin setup
- Emergency contact, if your clinic wants this for site access or lone-working situations
Option 2: Identity verification and right-to-work support   Record enough information to verify the person you are engaging   Due diligence
- Photo ID type and reference number
- ID check completed by, and date checked
- Proof of address, if your internal process requires it
- PPS Number only if genuinely needed for tax/payroll-related administration; avoid collecting it unnecessarily
- If relevant to the role, confirmation the contractor is permitted to work in Ireland
Option 3: Tax and payment details   Capture what finance needs to pay invoices correctly   Accounts payable
- Sole trader / individual contractor / company name
- Irish tax reference details, if provided and needed for finance records
- BIC, if required by your payment system
Option 4: Engagement and contract terms   Define what the contractor is being engaged to do   Scope and expectations
- Work location: onsite, remote, or hybrid
- Agreed rate: hourly, daily, project, or retainer
- Maximum approved budget or cap, if applicable
- Who approves timesheets, milestones, or invoices
Option 5: Confidentiality, data protection, and clinic access   Important for a healthcare setting   Information security
- Confirmation contractor will keep patient, staff, donor, and operational information confidential
- Whether the contractor will access personal data or special category health data
- Minimum access needed to systems, files, premises, and devices
- Data protection acknowledgment and privacy notice receipt
- Return or deletion of clinic data at end of engagement
- Incident reporting contact for data breach or security concern
Option 6: Insurance, compliance, and safeguarding checks   Useful where the role creates operational risk   Risk management
- Professional indemnity insurance details, if relevant
- Public liability insurance details, if relevant
- Policy number, insurer, and expiry date
- Garda vetting or safeguarding checks, if the role involves regulated activity or vulnerable persons
Records to Keep and Retention Notes

This is administrative guidance only; your clinic should align retention periods with its internal policy, Irish legal obligations, tax/accounting rules, HR practices, and data protection requirements.
- Retention points to build into the form or process:
- state why each category of data is collected
- set a retention period tied to contract end and statutory obligations
- securely delete or anonymize data when no longer needed
- keep a note of deletion/review dates
- “I understand my information will be used for contractor administration, payment, compliance, and recordkeeping in line with the clinic’s privacy notice and retention policy.”
Admin Notes for an Irish Nonprofit Clinic
Keep the form short and pair it with:
- a bank details form if you prefer to separate finance data
- an access checklist for email, systems, building access, and record return on exit
For a clinic setting, only collect health-related or vetting-related information if the role genuinely requires it.
